SM18A-A4.note: 8x−21=k, x=4 -> k=11; coefficient 8≠0 so no second no-solution value, exclusive. DESIGN FLAW: the +3 term is 3(x−4) after clearing, which is 0 at the excluded value, so k = (5x−9) at x=4 = 11 with the +3 ignored entirely. The naive 'k equals the other numerator at the hole' method lands on the key. Roles: −21 (candidate x=0), 23 (3x instead of 3(x−4)), −53 (x=−4) all real slips but none defensible. Desmos slider bypasses. Standard Bluebook shape, plays medium.

SM18A-A5.note: Distance from (a,−9) to x−y−3=0 is |a+6|/sqrt2 = 5sqrt2 -> a=4 or −16. Rejection verified: a=−16 spans x∈[−23.07,−8.93], misses x=0; a=4 spans [−3.07,11.07], contains 0. SM18A-B2.free_elimination: tidy-answer heuristic strikes the two decimals 6.8 and 8.5 (not formal); no sign/magnitude strike
SM18A-B2.note: 3(x−1)=−2(x−31), x=13; check 2^36 both sides. Distractor paths recomputed: 6.8 (−2x+31), 8.5 (base 2^−1), 11 (8=4² with exponent −(x−31)) all reproduce. This is the standard common-base exponential equation, a Bluebook medium; Desmos solves instantly. Not hard.

SM18A-B3.free_elimination: both roots negative => sum −(k−15)/3 < 0 => k > 15, strikes 7 by sign alone; 23 and 25 form an adjacent pair, key is the far outlier
SM18A-B3.note: (k−15)² = 16(2k−10) -> k²−62k+385=0 -> k=7 or 55. Rejection verified: k=7 gives (3x−2)(x−2), roots 2/3 and 2 positive; k=55 gives (3x+10)(x+10), roots −10/3, −10, ratio 3, both negative. Weak distractors: k=23 gives 3x²+8x+36 (disc −368) and k=25 gives 3x²+10x+40 (disc −380) — NEITHER has real roots, so the stem's own 'two real solutions' kills both on a discriminant check. Back-substituting k=55 factors cleanly, so option-testing reaches the key. Genuine Vieta decision point though; hard, bypassable.

SM18A-B4.free_elimination: k=5 is visible without algebra (identical fractions leave 0=7); k=12=5+7 is the coefficient-cancel value; key = 5 + (5+7), a sum of printed constants
SM18A-B4.note: (k−12)x=−21; k=12 -> 0=−21; k≠12 -> x=21/(12−k)=3 -> k=5. Both verified. Distractors 19/31 (sign error on 7(x−3)), 60 (product). The two-mechanism structure is real, but one of the two values is a printed coefficient (k=5 makes the equation read 0=7 on sight), and the other is the visible sum 5+7. A student who never clears denominators can get 17 from 'the fractions cancel at k=5' plus 'coefficients match at k=12'. That is the correct structure rather than a wrong method, so key stands; hard-minus.

SM18A-B5.note: a(x−3)²(x+2)(x+1), 18a=−6, a=−1/3, f(1)=(−1/3)(4)(3)(2)=−8. Distractor paths recomputed: −12 (no multiplicity, a=1), −18 (double zero at −2, a=1/2), −32 ((x+3)², a=−1/3) all reproduce. SM18A-B6.note: Vertex x=4, p(4)=−49, k=49, solutions 4 and roots of x²−8x−82 (sum 8), total 12.
